pr_body:
Logging v2 highlights
----------------------------
- `log_strdup` no longer needed!!
- logging `long long`, `float` and `double` is now possible!!
- hex dumps with formatted strings
- Self-contained messages (even transient strings are there)
- 32/64 bit timestamp
- better memory utilization - ~20% more messages fit in the logging buffer
- 6x faster logging from userspace!
- overall simplified implementation

API changes
-----------------
No change in logging API! Add `CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_DEFFERED=y` to run sample with new version. Only backend API extended with a function for processing v2 messages. PR updates following backends to support v2:
- uart
- shell
- adsp
- rtt
- native_posix

To be added later: bluetooth monitor, net, spinel, swo, xtensa sim

Internals
------------
It is utilizing cbprintf packages (#30675, #31102) to create self-contained log message. Using `_Generic` feature of C11, it is possible to act based on types of arguments. It is used to determine when formatted string requires time consuming, runtime package creation and when log message can be created as simple serialization of the arguments. When  `char *` arguments are present in the log message then package is created at runtime. This includes copying into a message any string argument which is from rw memory.

Additionally, log messages are no longer stored as fragmented chunks allocated from a memslab. They are stored in a circular buffer. This ensures that log message is not fragmented and improves memory utilization. Circular buffer is somehow generic multi producer, single consumer packet buffer (`lib/os/mpsc_pbuf`). Additional requirement is to support overwrite mode where oldest packets are dropped when new message cannot be allocated. MPSC packet buffer uses alloc, commit, claim, free sequence to avoid copying. Additionally, it has functions optimized for storing single word and single word + pointer packets. It is forseen that those will be used by the tracing to logger functionality.

It pends currently on #33567 being solved. PR contains temporary workaround to get CI green.

PR content
---------------
- mpsc packet buffer
- new log_msg2 implementation
- adaptation of the logger to support both version
- adaptation of  some logger backends to support v2 api

Fixes #26170
Fixes #18351
Fixes #26246
Fixes #30353
pr_comments: @andyross following approach is used: logging operates with a circular packet buffer (contrary to list of fragmented messages allocated from memslab). When logging is processing it passes the pointer to the message from the packet buffer to each backend. Call to the backend is synchronous so logging expects that when it returns message is no longer used by the backend. Backend has two option: block the logging thread and process the message or copy the message to its own memory and return.

PR is ready for review. I recommend to read logging documentation first as it highlights the differences between v1 and v2.

@jukkar I've applied your comments.

@dcpleung I've updated documentation with description of log message and cbprintf package content.

@nashif @dcpleung I've added dedicated section for log strings `log_strings_sections`. I've been playing a bit with `objcopy` and tried to remove that section but removing is just filling given section with 0's. It would need to be placed at the end probably. Or maybe you have some other ideas.

@nordic-krch Thank you. I have updated #30539 on top of this.

As for removing the section, it will probably require some linker magic. For example, on boards that is flashed with a .bin file, the log string section can be put into non-existing memory (thus won't appear in the final .bin file). But it still exists in the ELF file so we can extract the strings. On QEMU, this won't work because it will try to copy everything from ELF file into memory.

When long double is used but `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_PACKAGE_LONGDOUBLE=n`, there are bunch of compilation errors on the log macros themselves, and the error message about needing to enable the kconfig is buried among others. Just wondering if it is possible to get rid of the other errors with some macro magic?

Also, long double does not seem to work. `%Lf` is printed literally, but not the value. Maybe some other kconfig is needed besides `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_PACKAGE_LONGDOUBLE`?

> Also, long double does not seem to work. `%Lf` is printed literally, but not the value. Maybe some other kconfig is needed besides `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_PACKAGE_LONGDOUBLE`?

cbprintf_complete doesn't format long double, because there's no standard definition of how many bits it is and so there's no way to interpret it.  It gets flagged as unsupported when the length modifier is parsed.

> Just wondering if it is possible to get rid of the other errors with some macro magic?

Unfortunately, i don't see a way to do that as each argument in any log must be analyzed there is no way to avoid for loop macro and that results in the nested compiler errors. I would say that we are lucky that using `_Generic` we can detect that at compile time.
@dcpleung as part of the work you are doing with dictionary-based logging, which needs to be coupled to this overhaul, could you please also review this PR and approve if appropriate?

CONFIG_LOG2 with floating point output

Here is the list of the required CONFIG to get the LOG2 for floating point working.

**It is mandatory to set `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_A_SUPPORT=y`** to get `%f` and `%g` working! And `%a` is working also ;-).

```
CONFIG_LOG=y
CONFIG_LOG2_MODE_DEFERRED=y

CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC=y
CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_FLOAT_PRINTF=y

CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_A_SUPPORT=y

```

> **It is mandatory to set `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_A_SUPPORT=y`** to get `%f` and `%g` working! And `%a` is working also ;-).

No. CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_A_SUPPORT is for ... %a.

%f and %g just need CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_SUPPORT.

THanks for clarification. I have overlooked the `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_SUPPORT` flag.
`CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_A_SUPPORT` depends on and sets the `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_SUPPORT` flag.

So at least one of them has to set to get some output.
Just a note, `CONFIG_CBPRINTF_FP_SUPPORT` defaults to `y` when `CONFIG_FPU` is enabled so when FPU is in use you shouldn't need any additional explicit configuration.

issue_context.title: Printing 64-bit values in LOG_DBG
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
`LOG_DBG` does not seem to correctly output the value of uint64 variables when the value is larger than 32 bits.
I expect values of 2^^32 and larger to be printed as the value they are.
What happens is that the value 0 (zero) is printed instead.

For comparison, `printk` does print these values correctly, as does `printf` (when using NEWLIB).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

The code I made to reproduce this can be found here:
https://github.com/asbjornsabo/zephyr/tree/printf_64bit/samples/printf_64bit

The code in question is:
```
void main(void)
{
	uint64_t id = 1;
	uint8_t startshift = 30;
	uint8_t endshift = 34;
	uint8_t shift;

	id = id << startshift;

	for( shift = startshift; shift < endshift; shift++) {
		LOG_DBG("debug: The value of \"shift\" is %d, the value of \"id\" is 0x%llx\n", shift, id);
		printk("printk: The value of \"shift\" is %d, the value of \"id\" is 0x%llx\n", shift, id);
		printf("printf: The value of \"shift\" is %d, the value of \"id\" is 0x%llx\n", shift, id);
		id = id << 1;
	}
}
```
My prj.conf has
```
CONFIG_SERIAL=y
CONFIG_UART_NRFX=y
CONFIG_LOG=y
CONFIG_LOG_BACKEND_UART=y
CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL=4
CONFIG_DEBUG=y

CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC=y
CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC_NANO=n
```

What I do to reproduce is:
rm -rf build && cmake -H. -Bbuild -GNinja -DBOARD=nrf52840dk_nrf52840
cd build && ninja
(cd ..)
nrfjprog --eraseall --snr 683854931 && nrfjprog --program build/zephyr/zephyr.hex --verify --snr 683854931 && nrfjprog --reset --snr 683854931  
(Replace SNR with applicable value.)

The output I get is:
printk: The value of "shift" is 30, the value of "id" is 0x40000000
printf: The value of "shift" is 30, the value of "id" is 0x40000000
printk: The value of "shift" is 31, the value of "id" is 0x80000000
printf: The value of "shift" is 31, the value of "id" is 0x80000000
printk: The value of "shift" is 32, the value of "id" is 0x100000000
printf: The value of "shift" is 32, the value of "id" is 0x100000000
printk: The value of "shift" is 33, the value of "id" is 0x200000000
printf: The value of "shift" is 33, the value of "id" is 0x200000000
[00:00:00.004,608] <dbg> printf_64bit.main: debug: The value of "shift" is 30, the value of "id" is 0x40000000

[00:00:00.016,845] <dbg> printf_64bit.main: debug: The value of "shift" is 31, the value of "id" is 0x80000000

[00:00:00.029,022] <dbg> printf_64bit.main: debug: The value of "shift" is 32, the value of "id" is 0x0

[00:00:00.041,412] <dbg> printf_64bit.main: debug: The value of "shift" is 33, the value of "id" is 0x0


**Expected behavior**
The output I would expect is for LOG_DBG to output the same values as printk/printf.

**Impact**
As part of upcoming code for le-audio, I need to output 64 bit values for debugging.  I currently have self-made function for this.  This adds to the code, and I have been asked by the maintainer to replace this with more "standard" zephyr solutions.

**Screenshots or console output**
(See pasted otuput above.)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain (e.g Zephyr SDK, ...): Zephyr SDK 0.11.3
 - Commit SHA or Version used: Branched from master at 
31b19bf5383da87ee0e0e71157bfc7f547d9e4d7

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.
comments: @asbjornsabo I believe that the safe identifier to use is `PRIx64`
I have created similar enhancement req in the past #12098

The log mechanism uses the printk code (`snprintk()`, `vsnprintk()`, etc.) to manage format strings right? That code would need to be extended in order to support 64-bit integers on 32-bit systems, I don't believe it does currently.

The caveat is that printk() code is intentionally kept small since it's part of the core kernel, we want to be very careful about increasing its footprint (either code size or stack usage). Parts of the printf spec have been deliberately left out of it.

One possible alternative might be a config option for the log subsystem code to use the C library's `vsnprintf()` or `snprintf()` instead, which is fuller-featured (at the expense of code size and stack usage).

@jukkar correctly points out that the minimal libc printf() functions don't do this right either, but I don't see anything controversial about adding it there.

> @asbjornsabo I believe that the safe identifier to use is `PRIx64`
@carlescufi Plese explain what you mean by "safe identifier" and where I should use it.  (I assume you are not meaning as the format specifier?)

> The log mechanism uses the printk code (`snprintk()`, `vsnprintk()`, etc.) to manage format strings right? That code would need to be extended in order to support 64-bit integers on 32-bit systems, I don't believe it does currently.
> [...]
@andrewboie If the log mechanism uses printk code (I think I may have seen a vsnprintk or similar in there), why does `printk()` print the value correctly, and `LOG_DBG` not?  
(See the output - printk works.)

> @andrewboie If the log mechanism uses printk code (I think I may have seen a vsnprintk or similar in there), why does printk() print the value correctly, and LOG_DBG not?

that is the limitation of the logger. It stores each argument in `log_arg_t` which is `typedef unsigned long log_arg_t;` and  has 32 bit on 32 bit platforms. I need to check if storing on 64bits would solve the issue. If yes then i can add such option to the logger but it won't the the default since it will lead to increased log message size (more ram needed for log messages).

I tried to check if it is possible to redefine `log_arg_t` to `uint64_t` on 32bit platforms but i hit the issue with compilation warning when casting. Each log argument is casted to `log_arg_t` https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ad59e923e948605adf3baa44361cf1da2c22be50/include/logging/log_core.h#L201
and compiler complains when `void *` is casted to 64 bits. I don't know how to do that cast then. If anyone can suggest something?
`log_arg_t` I have seen lead to some very cryptic and misleading warning messages in existing code. What mechanism is this intended to support?
Are there any plans for progress on this?
Note that any solution to this would handle #18351 as well.  It's not a simple problem to solve; some history is in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/18351#issuecomment-522276594
